chunks: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan b. Shabib, who said:

I entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him) on the first day of Muharram. He said to me: O son of Shabib! Are you fasting? I said: No. He said: Verily this day is the day on which Zakariyya (peace be upon him) called upon his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: "My Lord, grant me good offspring from Your presence; surely You are the Hearer of prayers" (1). So He answered him and ordered the angels, and they called out to Zakariyya while he was standing in prayer in the prayer-niche: "Surely God gives you glad tidings of Yahya" (2). So whoever fasts this day and then calls upon God, the Mighty and Majestic, God will answer him as He answered Zakariyya (peace be upon him).

Then he said: O son of Shabib! Muharram is the month in which the people of the pre-Islamic era (Jahiliyya) would prohibit oppression and fighting due to its sanctity, yet this nation did not recognize the sanctity of its month nor the sanctity of its Prophet (may God bless him and his family). They killed his offspring in this month, captured his women, and plundered his provisions. May God never forgive them for that.

O son of Shabib! If you were to cry over anything, then cry over Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him), for he was slaughtered like the ram is slaughtered. Eighteen men from the people of his house, the like of whom are not to be found on the earth, were killed with him. The seven heavens and the earths wept over his killing. Four thousand angels descended to the earth to help him, but they found that he had already been killed. So they remain at his grave, dishevelled and dusty, until the Qa'im rises; then they will be among his helpers. And their slogan is: "O vengeance for Husayn!"

O son of Shabib! My father narrated to me from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon him): Surely, when my grandfather Husayn (blessings of God upon him) was killed, the sky rained blood and red dust.

O son of Shabib! If you wept over Husayn (peace be upon him) to the extent that your tears came onto your cheeks, God will forgive all of your sins which you have committed, whether minor or major, whether little or excessive.
O son of Shabib! If it pleases you to meet God, the Mighty and Majestic, while there is no sin upon you, then visit Husayn (peace be upon him).
O son of Shabib! If it pleases you to reside in the erected chambers in Paradise along with the Prophet and his family (blessings of God upon them), then curse the killers of Husayn.

O son of Shabib! If it pleases you to have a reward like that of the one who was martyred with Husayn (peace be upon him), then whenever you mention him, say: "Oh, how I wish I had been with them, so I would have attained a great victory!"

O son of Shabib! If it pleases you to be with us in the highest stages of the Gardens, then grieve over our sorrow and be happy in our happiness. And you must keep to our wilaya, for surely if a man were to befriend a stone, God would raise him with it on the Day of Resurrection (1).

key_terms.الحسين: Husayn - Imam Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.القائم: al-Qa'im - the Awaited One who will rise to establish justice
key_terms.المحرم: Muharram - the first month of the Islamic calendar, a sacred month
key_terms.الملائكة: angels - celestial beings who descended to help Husayn
key_terms.زكريا: Zakariyya - Prophet Zechariah who prayed for offspring
key_terms.ولايتنا: our wilaya - loyalty and guardianship of the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the rewards of mourning Husayn and fasting on the first of Muharram?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated on the first day of Muharram, Imam al-Rida (as) instructs al-Rayyan b. Shabib about the spiritual significance of fasting on Muharram 1st, linking it to Prophet Zakariyya's prayer for offspring (Quran 3:38-39). The Imam then delivers an impassioned exhortation about mourning Imam Husayn (as), recounting the cosmic grief of the heavens and earth at his martyrdom, the four thousand angels still waiting at his grave, and the spiritual rewards for weeping, visiting his shrine, cursing his killers, and maintaining loyalty (wilaya) to the Ahl al-Bayt. This teaching was delivered in 367 AH by Shaykh al-Saduq upon returning from visiting the Shrine of al-Rida, reflecting the deeply personal significance of Muharram commemorations in Shia devotional life.
